item.title: Ice-T’s Producer Says Twitch Remix Helped Revive His Rap Album
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ice-T's producer Charlemagne explains how a remix and support from Twitch DJs helped bring his rap album back into focus.
item.content:encoded:
Ice-T reconsidered making a rap album after producer Charlemagne remixed one of their earlier collaborations, according to the producer’s new account of their work together.

In a November 14 interview with RapIndustry, Charlemagne said Ice-T had expressed interest in recording an album before pulling back. He encouraged the rapper and made a remix that received attention from Twitch DJs.

“When he saw that, along with his peers in his age bracket making comebacks, he became convinced to do this new album,” Charlemagne said.

The resulting project, “Criminal Migraine,” arrived August 17, ending the gap between Ice-T’s solo studio albums that began after 2006’s “Gangsta Rap.” His official website currently sells the album as a $20 digital download, with no physical product included in that purchase.

Charlemagne produced seven tracks on the album, including the title song, “It’s What You Say,” “Hardcore MF” and “The Hate Is Real.” PA. Dre produced 10 tracks, while Afrika Islam returned to work with Ice-T on “No Competition.”

The collaborations extended beyond the production credits. Treach appears on three songs, including “Keep It Gangster,” and Smoothe Da Hustler contributes to “You Can Get It,” “The Hate Is Real” and “Lost My Mind.”

Ice-T had already described his renewed interest in recording during a July interview with AllHipHop. He pointed to Nas and Raekwon as artists whose continued output made him feel connected to rap again.

He also explained that storytelling remained his focus rather than adopting a different style. The album’s subjects included betrayal and growing older, with “To Be A Man” addressing the experiences he wanted to discuss at this stage of his life.

In that earlier conversation with Chuck Creekmur, Ice-T laid out his plan to sell downloads through his own website rather than release the project through streaming services. He described using social media to direct listeners toward his site and building a closer relationship with paying fans.

During his years between solo rap albums, Ice-T continued recording with Body Count and playing Fin Tutuola on “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.”

Charlemagne said his brother first connected them by handing Ice-T a beat CD during a supermarket encounter.

item.title: Adam22 Details What Cops Told Him About Chrisean Rock Attack
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Adam22 says he hopes to get Chrisean Rock arrested by the police and pursue a lawsuit to boot.
item.content:encoded:
Adam22 sounds mighty confident about a soon-to-be-arrested Chrisean Rock.

The No Jumper founder says he made good on his promise to hit up the Inglewood Police Department following his physical confrontation with Chrisean Rock at “Wild ’N Out.” “I’m going to the Inglewood Police Department tomorrow to report Chrisean. She should be arrested some time this week. We have to keep these violent freaks off the street,” he said.

That was his announcement and now he says he did the deed. We don’t have a report or an arrest warrant so we’ll have to take his word on it.

Look below for his words and what he says they told him at the police department.

“I’m hearing reports she is planning on leaving the country. That might slow down her arrest but it won’t stop the lawsuit,” he said emphatically.

Now, who supplied these travel updates?

Anyway…

For those catching up, the November 12 confrontation followed Adam mocking Chrisean’s parenting during the live show at Intuit Dome. She struck him, and he subsequently described swelling and concerns about his ability to work. Their previous public dispute supplied plenty of hostility before either entered that venue.

My question is whether Adam’s next update comes with paperwork. He is discussing a lawsuit as though it already has a reserved parking space, but the reviewed reporting does not establish a filed civil case.

Nobody should have to accept being hit as part of a comedy booking. Still, predicting somebody’s arrest is a substantial claim. For this corner of Hip-Hop media, the next meaningful development will come from an arrest of Chrisean. I am thinking she will get a slap on the wrist. Even if he made it a civil matter, it’s small money.

item.title: Beyonce’s BeyGOOD Gives $50,000 To Teen Literacy & Publishing Program
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Beyonce's BeyGOOD awards $50,000 to Reach, Incorporated as its teen authors prepare for a November 19 book launch.
item.content:encoded:
Beyonce‘s BeyGOOD Foundation has awarded $50,000 to Reach, Incorporated, a Washington, D.C., nonprofit that trains teenagers to tutor younger students and helps them publish children’s books.

The foundation announced the grant November 9, ahead of Reach’s annual celebration of its teen authors. The organization’s 2026 Book Launch Party is scheduled for November 19.

“BeyGOOD is excited to award a $50,000 grant to Reach, Incorporated!” the foundation wrote in its announcement. Its accompanying posts described a program that combines literacy instruction with mentorship.

During the school year, the teenagers visit elementary schools twice a week to tutor students, according to BeyGOOD. The foundation also highlighted their work with professionals during Reach’s Summer Leadership Academy.

That summer program gives participants several ways to contribute to a book. Reach says its tutors can write, illustrate, research and take photographs through the Teen Publishing Project, producing material that remains available after the academy ends.

Reach describes its broader mission as developing readers and leaders by preparing teens to serve as tutors and role models. The nonprofit recruits and trains young people facing academic and social challenges, then hires them to work with elementary students who also need support.

Its approach includes teaching tutors to break down passages, identify important components and guide younger readers toward understanding the text. Reach says the model is intended to improve literacy for both groups, rather than focusing only on the children receiving tutoring.

The grant follows years of education programs under BeyGOOD. According to its official history, Beyonce launched the initiative during her 2013 Mrs. Carter Show World Tour.

In 2017, her Formation Scholars Award supported women studying creative arts, music, literature and African American studies at four colleges. The following year, the Homecoming Scholars Award supported students attending historically Black colleges and universities.

For the upcoming book celebration, Reach says attendees will be able to meet its tutors and community members while recognizing the new teen authors. The event will feature books produced through the Teen Publishing Project.

Reach’s November 19 launch party runs from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at Washington’s True Reformer Building.

Archival interview: BeyGOOD discusses its education programs on CBS Mornings in 2023.

item.title: Flo Rida Backs Thanksgiving Food Drive For Miami Gardens Families
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Flo Rida supports holiday grocery help in Miami Gardens as local partners continue their annual Thanksgiving drive.
item.content:encoded:
Flo Rida backed a Miami Gardens food giveaway Saturday, according to CBS Miami.

The November 14 drive was organized around Thanksgiving baskets at Studio 183. Partner Kelley | Uustal outlined the plans in a November 4 announcement, describing packages with turkey, stuffing and other food intended to serve ten people.

The law firm said this marked its third consecutive year supporting the rapper’s annual drive. Its announcement identified Strong Arm, International Music Group and 103.5 The Beat among the participating organizations.

“Staying connected to the communities we serve, from Broward to Miami-Dade, is part of who we are,” Kelley | Uustal said.

Other listed partners included Miller/Jacobs, Reginald A. Mathis & Associates and the Beta Beta Lambda chapter of Alpha Phi Alpha. Volunteers were scheduled to assemble the holiday baskets at the venue.

Flo Rida’s work with his longtime manager and business partner, Freezy, also received congressional recognition this fall. Representative Frederica Wilson entered a tribute to Freezy into the Congressional Record on October 6.

Wilson described Big Dreams for Kids, which Freezy co-founded with Flo Rida, and its football, cheerleading and track programs. She also cited Freezy’s Thanksgiving food assistance and Christmas toy distributions.

“Every Thanksgiving, Freezy feeds community members, ensuring families in need have proper holiday meals,” Wilson said.

The same tribute documented the partners’ $10 million purchase of Miami Gardens’ Cloverleaf Shopping Plaza in 2023. Wilson said the property had received improvements under their ownership, including changes to maintenance and security.

Separately, AllHipHop reported that Flo Rida was announced as the headliner for the November 14 Best Buddies Miami Gala at Mana Wynwood, supporting programs for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

Wilson’s tribute also identified Studio 183 as part of Freezy’s business portfolio.

item.title: Westside Gunn Holds Off On 4th Rope TV Deal To Build Its Value
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Westside Gunn says television can wait while he expands 4th Rope into more cities and raises the wrestling company's worth.
item.content:encoded:
Westside Gunn says 4th Rope could land on television in 2027, but he wants to make his wrestling promotion more valuable before bringing in outside partners. The Griselda founder disclosed the offer while outlining his next moves beyond recording albums.

“We’ve been approached already. It can be on TV in 2027 if I took the deal right now,” Westside Gunn told Billboard. “But right now, I’m keeping it underground, and building it up a little more, so it’s worth more.”

Gunn said investors and potential partners have already contacted him. He wants to reach additional major cities independently before making that commitment, with Los Angeles among the markets still on his list.

The company is aiming for roughly one event a month rather than a weekly schedule. Gunn described a traveling operation that has brought its shows to Paris Fashion Week, SXSW, Philadelphia and Las Vegas, mixing wrestling with live music and clothing. Smoke DZA shares the work behind the scenes, with Gunn saying the two even book flights together for talent.

He also designs merchandise around each stop instead of bringing an identical collection everywhere. His examples included reworking vintage Denver sports jerseys with Griselda’s scorpion imagery to connect the clothes to the host city.

“We haven’t did L.A. yet. We still got to hit big markets. Let’s keep doing what we doing,” Westside Gunn said.

The expansion plans follow his meeting with WWE president Nick Khan, which ended a public dispute between the rapper and the wrestling company. Gunn had previously said he was removed from a Buffalo Raw event and objected to complaints over wrestling references in his work.

In the new interview, Gunn credited a direct conversation with Khan for resolving the conflict. He said the executive appreciated his promotion of WWE, while declining to spell out any forthcoming collaboration.

Music remains part of the business as Gunn rolls out Heelmatic through Griselda and Mass Appeal. The rapper said he plans to keep that album’s campaign running through February before moving to Awesome God 3 in the spring.

Gunn also revealed plans to work with Benny The Butcher on Tana Talk 5.

item.title: Giggs Shooting Case Ends In Acquittal For Accused Lookout
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Giggs shooting trial clears an alleged scout as defense lawyers challenge phone evidence and claims about gang ties.
item.content:encoded:
Giggs was the alleged target in a London shooting case that has ended with one defendant unanimously cleared.

A jury at the Old Bailey rejected firearm, ammunition and grievous bodily harm charges against the man following a four-week trial. His barrister’s chambers announced the verdict on November 9, describing a prosecution case built around alleged scouting for the attackers.

The shooting followed the rapper’s 2025 appearance with DJ AG in Peckham, according to Garden Court Chambers. A bystander sustained a serious foot injury, while prosecutors accused the defendant of checking the area and passing information to people inside a vehicle.

The defense did not dispute that he briefly entered the vehicle. Instead, the man said he was talking innocently with his cousin and denied helping prepare an attack.

Barrister Tetevi Davi challenged the prosecution using phone records, location information and forensic material, the chambers said.

Its account also says questioning of a gang expert established that the defendant had no gang membership or association. The charges required prosecutors to prove intent to endanger life or to cause grievous bodily harm, respectively.

The injury had previously featured in a January investigation into London’s gun crime, when a detective described recovering a bullet from the bystander’s sock.

The victim’s foot bones were shattered after the bullet ricocheted, according to the officer’s account of the shooting.

Giggs has previously described years of police interference with his performances, including concerts canceled shortly before he could take the stage. In a 2024 interview, he said accusations of gang activity kept him from performing normally for roughly a decade.

The rapper recalled arranging private appearances and transporting audiences by coach, only to have authorities discover the shows.

Those restrictions were separate from the visa difficulties that delayed his first American tour, which eventually brought him to nine cities.

During that tour, Giggs spoke with AllHipHop before his Los Angeles appearance about valuing live crowds over streaming statistics. His Zero Tolerance album featured American collaborators including Jadakiss, Dave East and 21 Savage alongside Popcaan.

Linda Okoli of Titan Solicitors instructed Davi in the recently concluded firearms trial.

item.title: Akon’s “Smack That” With Eminem Earns Diamond Certification
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Akon's "Smack That" reaches Diamond status as "I Wanna Love You" and "Don't Matter" receive six-times Platinum certifications.
item.content:encoded:
Akon‘s “Smack That” collaboration with Eminem has reached Diamond status, according to the RIAA’s latest official certification records. The organization lists the Universal single at 1X Diamond, with an award date of November 13, 2026.

The same database update puts “I Wanna Love You” and “Don’t Matter” at six-times Platinum. All three songs appeared on Konvicted, Akon’s second album, which arrived in 2006.

Diamond recognizes 10 million qualifying U.S. units. The RIAA counts downloads and on-demand audio and video streams toward digital single certifications, using a conversion of 150 streams for one download. A third-party auditing firm reviews the applications and supporting figures.

“Smack That” had already made chart history during its original release. As AllHipHop reported in 2006, the song jumped from No. 95 to No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100, the biggest climb in the chart’s history at that time.

Its first week of digital sales totaled 67,000 downloads, putting it at No. 6 on the Hot Digital Songs chart. Akon discussed the pressure of following that success in an interview with AllHipHop during the album’s rollout. The rise surpassed “Breaking Free,” the Vanessa Hudgens, Zac Efron and Andrew Seeley recording that had moved from No. 86 to No. 4 earlier that year, setting the previous record.

“I just feel like as long as I’m working hard, and putting out good music, it shouldn’t be a problem,” Akon said.

Akon later described the Detroit recording sessions in a 2015 interview with The Charlatan. He said he traveled there hoping to work with Eminem and initially went to the studio late, expecting the rapper to record at night.

Instead, he discovered Eminem kept regular daytime studio hours. Akon said the two connected immediately, and that a strip-club visit the previous night helped inspire the words when he heard the track.

The song also earned Akon and Eminem a nomination for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration at the 2007 Grammy Awards. Konvicted received a Best Contemporary R&B Album nomination the following year.

“I Wanna Love You,” Akon’s collaboration with Snoop Dogg, also received a 2008 Grammy nomination for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration.

item.title: Ludacris & Organized Noize Get New Walk Of Fame Date
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Ludacris and Organized Noize move toward a February ceremony after FIFA preparations disrupted their Atlanta honors.
item.content:encoded:
Ludacris and Organized Noize have a new date for their Black Music & Entertainment Walk of Fame ceremony after the Atlanta event was postponed in June.

An organizers’ announcement dated November 13 sets the induction for February 11, 2027. Davido, Bishop Paul S. Morton, Jack the Rapper and former Atlanta Mayor Maynard H. Jackson are also listed in the class.

The announcement, distributed through outlets including The Chronicle News, places the celebration during Black History Month. Signia by Hilton Atlanta is named as the host hotel.

Ludacris’ selection had already been announced for the 2026 class, with a June 1 ceremony planned near Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The new announcement retains the honorees named for that earlier event.

In a June 10 statement, organizers said fencing associated with FIFA preparations had cut off access to portions of the Walk of Fame site. The installation prevented them from holding the ceremony as planned, although other Black Music Week events went ahead.

“The Walk of Fame monument is more than a destination,” co-founder Michael Mauldin said in that statement. He specifically named Ludacris and Jackson while promising another date for their celebration.

The Walk of Fame installs its Crown Jewel of Excellence emblems at Martin Luther King Jr. Drive and Northside Drive. Its founders are Catherine Brewton, Demmette Guidry and Mauldin, and the project involves the Black American Music Association and Black American Music Foundation.

Previous honorees include Outkast, Missy Elliott, Nas, Lil Wayne, Usher and Mary J. Blige.

Organized Noize formed in the early 1990s, bringing together Rico Wade, Ray Murray and Sleepy Brown. Their production credits include work with Outkast, Goodie Mob and TLC, including “So Fresh, So Clean” and “Waterfalls.”

Wade died in April 2024 at 52. His work included Outkast’s 1994 debut, Southernplayalisticadillacmuzik, and collaborations with Ludacris and Killer Mike. Organized Noize and the Dungeon Family issued a joint statement mourning his death.

The June postponement did not cancel the separate Black American Music Awards at Morehouse College’s Ray Charles Performing Arts Center. That event honored Jermaine Dupri, Anthony Hamilton, Kenny Lattimore and Jagged Edge.

The Black American Music Association was founded in 2017.

item.title: Michael Jai White Says He Beat Up A Rapper, But Who Was It?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Michael Jai White’s claim that he beat up an unnamed rapper has sparked a guessing game.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Jai White has handed us all a guessing game with his claim that he once beat up a rapper, and apparently the name is going to cost us extra.

Who was it? That is the question. So far, I haven’t found a verified answer, but the story is circulating in online discussions where people are already trying to solve the mystery.

Here is the story below. Watch this and tell me what you think.

We have a claim. We have an unidentified rapper. We do not have enough information to put a face on the receiving end.

Still, you can understand why this has people curious. Usually, a rapper’s alleged fight comes with seventeen camera angles, a blurry security recording and somebody selling an interview before the swelling goes down.

I do believe this was back in the day as well. So, he did not give it a year, but it most certainly FELT like it was back in the day.

Was this somebody famous enough that the revelation would make everybody gasp? Would we recognize the name immediately? Those are questions, folks. I think it was probably a bum. I mean, there was no posse? No crew? Just a rapper all alone with MJW?

Personally, I want to know how the supposed confrontation even reached that point. What was said? What happened beforehand? Without those details, we cannot tell whether “beat up” describes a brief scuffle or something considerably more serious.

So, AllHipHop community, I’m passing this one to you.

For now, Michael Jai White has supplied the mystery. Tell me who you think it is.

item.title: Wiz Khalifa Offers Community Service In Romania As Court Weighs Cannabis Case
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiz Khalifa addresses Romanian judges by video, offering community service as his cannabis case heads toward a November 19 ruling.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa offered to perform community service in Romania during a November 12 court appearance, as judges reconsider the cannabis case that once carried a nine-month prison term.

The rapper joined the Bucharest Court of Appeal by video. Digi24 reported that he acknowledged wrongdoing and expressed regret during questioning lasting about 10 to 15 minutes.

Wiz told judges he had donated to organizations opposing drug use and would continue supporting them.

The original sentencing judges had treated his celebrity status as an aggravating factor, arguing that smoking cannabis publicly could encourage young people to view illegal drug use as acceptable, rather than treating the incident as private consumption alone.

Community service has not been announced as his punishment. The judges heard him after annulling the previous prison judgment on November 3, a ruling that reopened the prosecution’s appeal rather than ending the case.

The dispute has moved between courts and produced sharply different penalties. The Constanta Tribunal initially imposed a 3,600-lei criminal fine. Prosecutors from DIICOT, Romania’s organized-crime agency, challenged that outcome and secured a prison sentence from the Constanta Court of Appeal in December 2025.

That December ruling is the one Bucharest judges have now set aside. They also canceled the warrant authorizing enforcement of the sentence, according to the November 3 order reproduced by Romania’s national news agency AGERPRES.

An earlier attempt to overturn the sentence failed in February, when the Constanta appeal court rejected his annulment challenge as inadmissible.

Wiz’s lawyers had sought to move the annulment proceedings away from Constanta. Romania’s highest court granted that request in September, sending the matter to Bucharest before the latest hearings.

The underlying charge concerns possession for personal use, not drug trafficking. Prosecutors said the rapper had 18.53 grams of cannabis and a cannabis cigarette at the Beach, Please! festival in Costinesti on July 13, 2024.

Police took him in after his onstage performance, but he was subsequently released and left Romania. Prosecutors brought the case to trial in October 2024.

The court set November 19 for “deliberation, pronouncement and drafting,” according to its short order.
